value.rationale: A symmetric intersection of congruent circles is a canonical natural one-parameter family of centrally symmetric convex bodies, not an artificial slice. Its exact maximal inscribed-triangle area is a geometric extremal invariant connected to critical lattice-covering triangles. The theorem gives a uniform trigonometric formula with all equality cases across the whole strict-overlap range. The smooth-branch exclusion requires a substantive second-variation argument, while the two-reflection classification is not supplied by the previously solved canonical special case. It neither merely recounts a table nor claims a false general downstream theorem.
